body: The spec is methodologically more careful than the project description (fold-wise PCA fitting, permutation within folds, leave-one-study-out CV), but it rests on one unexamined load-bearing assumption it never tests or even checks: that truly paired samples — the same biological specimens with both 16S and metabolomics — exist across SRA and MetaboLights. FR-002 demands 'a strict one-to-one sample match,' yet nothing in the spec or the parent project establishes that such cross-repository pairing exists at all; the far more common situation is that microbiome and metabolomics studies of herbivore stress are separate experiments on different plants. Assumption 1 ('n ≥ 30') gestures at this but sample count is not the issue — sample *identity* is. If pairing is impossible, every downstream requirement is untestable, and the spec should make sample-pairing verification itself an acceptance scenario rather than an assumption. Second, there are internal contradictions the spec should resolve: FR-004 mandates 5-fold CV while FR-012 and US-2 mandate leave-one-study-out; these are different protocols and the permutation test (FR-011) is specified 'within each CV fold' without saying which. FR-013 is also self-contradictory: a 'multi-output Random Forest regressor' that 'predicts each defense metabolite individually' is either one model with multiple outputs or many single-output models — the two give different per-metabolite R² aggregation. Finally, SC-006 inverts its own logic: 'performance does not drop dramatically under leave-one-study-out CV' is stated as the validation criterion, but a large drop under LOSO is precisely the *detection* of study-driven signal — the criterion as written would pass exactly when batch effects are masked by 5-fold CV. And SC-007's claim that 'the resulting p-value distribution is uniform under the null' is asserted as a validation outcome but no test is specified to establish it.
